subject: french
source_note: Topic structure follows the CCEA GCSE French specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Context 1: Identity, Lifestyle & Culture
units.blurb: Self, family, technology, leisure and celebrations

units.name: Context 2: Local, National & Global Interest
units.blurb: Local area, community, global issues and travel

units.name: Context 3: School, Studies & Work
units.blurb: School life, activities, part-time jobs and future plans

topics.name: Myself, Family & Relationships
topics.blurb: Family, friends, relationships and personal choices

topics.name: Social Media & New Technology
topics.blurb: Online communication, devices and their use

topics.name: Free Time, Leisure & Daily Routine
topics.blurb: Sport, hobbies, entertainment, food and daily life

topics.name: My Local Area & Environment
topics.blurb: Home, neighbourhood, town, region and country

topics.name: Social & Global Issues
topics.blurb: Health, lifestyle and caring for others and the environment

topics.name: My Studies & School Life
topics.blurb: Subjects, uniform, timetable, rules and regulations

topics.name: Extra-Curricular Activities
topics.blurb: Clubs, societies, events, trips and visits

topics.name: Part-Time Jobs & Money Management
topics.blurb: Evening and weekend work and work experience

topics.name: Listening
topics.blurb: Understanding spoken French and extracting key information

topics.name: Reading & Translation into English
topics.blurb: Understanding written texts and translating into English

topics.name: Writing & Translation into French
topics.blurb: Producing extended text and translating into French

connections.why: Talking about family naturally extends to shared free time and routines
Much modern leisure and entertainment happens through technology and media
Festivals, food and celebrations are a key part of cultural leisure
Describing your area builds the vocabulary for describing travel destinations
Local environment leads into wider social and environmental issues
Voluntary work connects to caring for others and the wider world
School subjects and clubs are described with overlapping vocabulary
Choices about studies lead into post-16 and career plans
Part-time work experience informs talk about future employment
Understanding spoken French is the basis for responding in conversation
Reading models of text supports accurate, well-structured writing
Translation skills work in both directions between French and English
Personal topics are the staple content of the speaking assessment
Opinion topics give the substance for extended written responses
Authentic cultural texts develop reading comprehension
Travel scenarios are common contexts for listening tasks
